correctness.rationale: Complete-history transition s/k^q is exact. Mean product, bounded moments, gamma infinite product, Bonferroni stabilization asymptotic and Yule stochastic domination were reconstructed with boundary conditions n>=2. Exhaustive independent parent-vector enumeration matched every rational recurrence for q=2 (n<=7), q=3 (n<=5); 375 rational assertions plus 80 numerical analytic checks passed.

evidence: Bäumler et al. (arXiv:2609.30098v1) give an unlabelled matching lower bound n^{0.83}; it allows matchings different from fixed birth labels.
Baur (arXiv:1407.2508v1) Theorem 1 assumes common retention p(n)→1 and normalizes macroscopic cluster sizes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A size lower bound for optimally matched unlabelled subtrees cannot determine the distribution of the much stricter birth-label-preserving rooted intersection. Neither reported theorem dominates this exact finite-state/gamma/asymptotic family. The inaccessible 2026 full text is an explicit residual risk.
searches: "On the largest common subtree of uniform attachment trees" "Ulam–Harris" root common

evidence: Individual parent-edge agreement indicators are independent with probabilities 1/k, yielding logarithmically many matches for two trees. The root-connected shared paths require conditioning on the parent belonging to the already shared root component, changing the hazard to s/k^2.
Homogeneous recursive-tree percolation covers a different retention regime (arXiv:1407.2508v1, Section 2).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The known common-edge total and its generating function do not determine the parent locations or the connected root component, so do not imply this non-linear ancestor law. Deriving it requires the root-state transition followed by infinite-product and stabilization analysis.
searches: "recursive forest intersection of independent tree edge sets root component size finite versus logarithmically many identical parent edges"

evidence: For matching parent choices in independent recursive trees, age-indexed retention is k^{1-q} conditional on a uniform parent, whereas the root-cluster birth probability is s/k^q.
Baur (arXiv:1407.2508v1), pp. 1–6, defines uniform common edge-retention p(n), not edge-age retention.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact equivalent formulation is inhomogeneous recursive-tree bond percolation with birth-dependent retention; it is included and analyzed directly. Searches for that formulation and same-lineage counts identified homogeneous percolation but not an equivalent full theorem.

evidence: The inspected primary texts report homogeneous percolation cluster asymptotics and optimal common-subtree bounds, not tabulated distributions of the fixed-label common root component.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact database or table directly containing the Markov law with gamma stabilization product or sharp n^{-1} late-arrival constant was located. Non-discovery is not treated as proof of historical novelty.

originality.rationale: The exact birth-indexed common-root ancestry chain and its Gamma stabilization identity, polynomial late-arrival constant and exponential limit tail are not implied by the inspected uniform-retention recursive-tree percolation theorem or the reported optimal unlabelled common-subtree lower bound. Distinct statements and implications, not matching keywords, were compared. Full recent manuscript access and unindexed priority remain risks.
residual_risks: Full 2026 common-subtree manuscript could not be read; comparison is restricted to its abstract and accessible synopsis.
Older unindexed age-dependent recursive-forest or common-ancestry identities could be equivalent.
The exponential Yule tail bound is not claimed optimal.

value.rationale: The exact root-ancestry agreement component is a natural stringent genealogical similarity statistic across independent random growth histories. Gamma conditional stabilization and sharp late-agreement constants quantify permanent cessation, and an exponential tail contrasts meaningfully with logarithmically many isolated identical parents. The result is a structural asymptotic and complete law, not a relabelled count or arbitrary finite parameter slice.
